tasks.title: Port delegate.py process model to psutil (cross-platform)
tasks.objective: delegate.py launches, supervises and reaps Codex workers through psutil on both platforms: the ps-shelling and os.killpg are gone, preexec_fn is dropped, Popen branches creationflags by OS, and the fragile ps-lstart identity is retired.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the ps-shelling functions (_process_table, _process_start_identity, _process_is_zombie, _tagged_processes and the _descendants walk) with psutil: children(recursive=True), process_iter(['pid','ppid','create_time','environ','cmdline']), create_time() and status(). No `ps` subprocess call remains anywhere in delegate.py; the ps-lstart whitespace-normalized identity comparison is DELETED, not reimplemented (lesson normalize-ps-derived-identity) — identity is create_time() (float). The FORGE_PROCESS_TOKEN env-marker sweep uses process_iter(['environ']) and catches psutil.AccessDenied/NoSuchProcess, falling back to cmdline; only same-user workers are reaped.

Replace os.killpg termination (_process_group_alive, _signal_verified_process_group, _capture_spawn_identity escalation, _signal_identified_processes) with psutil terminate()/kill() over the leader + children(recursive=True), identity-guarded by create_time() (PID-reuse guard preserved: never signal a PID whose create_time differs from the recorded one).

launch_companion: drop preexec_fn; branch Popen creationflags — Windows subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, POSIX start_new_session=True; the recorded pgid stays the tree root psutil walks. blocked_termination_signals()/unblock_termination_signals_in_child remain (already no-op on Windows via the pthread_sigmask hasattr guard) — do not remove the guard.

delegations.jsonl schema/fields unchanged (pid, pgid, identity keep their shape; identity value moves from an lstart string to a create_time float — a format change internal to delegate.py, not a schema field change). _reconcile_stale_launches routes through the ported helpers with no separate Windows branch.

psutil is pinned in the harness's dependency surfaces so the ported tests and real delegations can import it: add `--with psutil` to FACTORY_TEST_CMD in .envrc (currently `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests -q`) and to the matching default suggestion string in factory/scripts/verify.py (the `uv run --with pytest ...` example ~line 36). There is no requirements manifest; these two command surfaces are the pins. Keep the change minimal and consistent (both surfaces gain the same `--with psutil`). Decision 0041 text refined if implementation reveals corrections; status stays proposed.

The ps-monkeypatch unit tests (the ones faking _process_table/_tagged_processes/killpg, e.g. around test_gates.py:7834/9864/11331/11340/11370/11445/11508/11574) migrate to psutil fakes and stay green; POSIX behavior observably byte-identical (launch/supervise/reap/lock-release). Full POSIX suite green.

LAZY psutil import (WIN-1 fcntl lesson): `import psutil` must NOT be at module top level. forge.py imports forge_cli.delegate UNCONDITIONALLY for every command, so a top-level psutil import breaks the ENTIRE CLI — including `forge doctor`, which is what installs psutil — when psutil is absent. Import psutil lazily inside the process functions that use it (mirroring the existing lazy `import fcntl` in _lock_file). A `from forge_cli import delegate` must succeed with psutil NOT installed; only actually launching/reaping a delegation touches psutil. Add a test asserting delegate imports cleanly without psutil (e.g. monkeypatch the import to fail and confirm module import still works).

pid_started stays a STRING in delegations.jsonl (schema factory/schemas/delegation.json UNCHANGED, out of scope): serialize the psutil create_time float via str(); the identity guard compares the serialized form (stable across calls) or parses both to float. Never signal a PID whose serialized create_time differs from the recorded one (PID-reuse guard preserved).

REGRESSION FIX — the port left 26 failures with THREE root causes, fix all: (1) DOMINANT: pid_started is being recorded as a FLOAT (create_time), which factory/schemas/delegation.json REFUSES ('pid_started must be str'), so every delegation that records a ledger row fails (test_delegate_records_ledger_entry, test_delegate_passes_with_fresh_task_grill, test_delegate_retry_reconciles_interrupted_running_launch, test_hook_allows_briefed_write_delegation, test_forge_fix_records_terra_high_write_delegation, test_next_names_delegation_step, etc.). Serialize pid_started with str() so the LEDGER field stays a string (schema unchanged); keep the create_time identity comparison internal (parse both to float, or compare the stable str form). (2) OBSOLETE ps-specific unit tests: tests that assert the OLD ps machinery are now meaningless and must be REMOVED, not migrated — notably test_process_identity_matches_the_process_table_on_single_digit_days (it guards the exact ps-lstart day-padding fragility this port DELETES) and test_process_table_failure_is_not_treated_as_an_empty_table if it asserts ps subprocess behavior. Delete tests that only tested removed ps internals; migrate tests that assert real reap/identity BEHAVIOR to psutil fakes (test_tagged_process_scan_skips_unreadable_environments / _permission_denied_candidates → psutil.AccessDenied fakes). (3) POSIX reap/termination must actually work via psutil: test_termination_signals_reap_companion_before_lock_release[*], test_stage_done_reaps_required_test_descendants / _verify_command_descendants, test_stage_done_termination_signal_reaps_active_proof[*], test_proof_reaps_spawn_when_process_identity_probe_fails[*], test_process_signal_revalidates_each_pid_identity, test_process_group_signal_requires_live_leader_identity, test_delegate_ignores_stale_lock_contents_when_no_process_holds_it — the psutil terminate()/kill() over children(recursive=True) with create_time identity must reap the real spawned trees on POSIX exactly as killpg did. AND the still-unfixed LAZY IMPORT (1): REMOVE the top-level `import psutil` (line ~35) — `from forge_cli import delegate` must succeed without psutil; import it lazily inside the process functions (like lazy `import fcntl`); a test must prove import-without-psutil succeeds. Target: the full delegation/process selector `-k 'delegat or process or terminat or reap or tagged or reconcile'` is GREEN with `--with psutil`, AND delegate imports clean without psutil.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "delegat or process or terminat or reap or tagged or reconcile"

tasks.reviewer_focus: The PID-reuse guard must survive the port — never signal a PID whose create_time differs from the recorded identity (the whole point of the old lstart check). No `ps` call may remain. AccessDenied/NoSuchProcess on Windows environ reads must be caught (a raise there would break the token sweep). POSIX launch/reap must be observably identical. Verify against committed HEAD after any multi-round rewrite (lesson repeated-full-file-rewrites-regress-prior-fixes). CI-blind: the Windows launch path is verified in WIN-3.2's E2E, not here.

tasks.title: Doctor psutil row + Windows delegation E2E + CI selector + docs
tasks.objective: psutil is a gated prerequisite the harness installs, a real delegation launch/supervise/reap is proven on windows-latest CI, and docs state Windows delegation is supported with the unelevated sandbox deferred.
acceptance_criteria: forge doctor gains a REQUIRED psutil row (import check); doctor --fix installs it (pip/uv, user scope, honest red row when it cannot) reusing the WIN-2 doctor-row + --fix patterns; fast_status stays subprocess-free (import check is a cheap importlib.util.find_spec, not an exec).

A NEW nt-appropriate delegation E2E in test_gates.py exercises the real Windows path: a delegation launches (records `running`), then the worker tree is terminated via the psutil path and the terminal `failed` row + delegation-lock release are asserted — the nt analog of the POSIX-signal test_termination_signals_reap_companion_before_lock_release (which stays POSIX-only). This nt test joins the windows-hook-gates explicit selector in factory-scaffold.yml (explicit node-id list per D-0020, -q last); every selector id must exist.

AC2: a test asserts the recorded .factory/delegations.jsonl argv carries --write (→ workspace-write) on Windows; docs/windows.md documents that Windows delegation is supported and that the unelevated sandbox is deferred (D-0021).
Full POSIX suite green; the WIN-2 init/adopt/upgrade propagation tests confirm the psutil dep manifest ships to clients; windows-hook-gates green on the PR (the real cross-platform proof).

doctor --fix psutil install target (learned in 3.1): install psutil for the INTERPRETER THAT RUNS forge (the one importing forge_cli.delegate), not an arbitrary python — on Windows the winget/py launcher's pip, on POSIX the running interpreter's pip. Handle a PEP-668 externally-managed environment gracefully: try `--user` and fall back to a clear named red row telling the user how (never silently `--break-system-packages`). The doctor row uses importlib.util.find_spec('psutil') (cheap, subprocess-free) so fast_status stays subprocess-free; the required red row when absent reuses the WIN-2 doctor-row + --fix patterns and names the manual `pip install psutil` fallback.

Review round: (1) find_spec only proves psutil is DISCOVERABLE, not that it IMPORTS (a stale/ABI/arch-incompatible install passes find_spec but fails `import psutil`). The AUTHORITATIVE doctor row must actually import psutil (try: import psutil; except Exception -> red) so an unusable install is caught; fast_status keeps the cheap find_spec as an OPTIMISTIC subprocess-free heuristic (WIN-2 fast_status-heuristic-vs-doctor-authoritative pattern) — doctor is the authority. (2) doctor --fix install must be venv-aware: `pip install --user` is REJECTED inside a virtualenv ('User site-packages are not visible in this virtualenv'). Detect a venv (sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix): in a venv install WITHOUT --user (into the venv); outside a venv use --user; a PEP-668 externally-managed environment falls to the honest named red row with the manual `pip install psutil` guidance. Test both: doctor red when psutil imports-but-is-broken (simulate import failure), and the install command shape is venv-correct.

Fix test_tagged_process_scan_falls_back_when_cached_environment_is_denied to reflect REAL psutil semantics: process_iter(['environ']) sets info['environ']=None when a process's environ cannot be read (psutil's as_dict swallows AccessDenied to None) — it does NOT return a dict whose .get() raises. Rewrite the test so the denied case is info['environ']=None (not a DeniedEnvironment that raises), asserting the cmdline() fallback still tags the process — which the CURRENT delegate.py already handles (isinstance(environment, dict) is False for None -> cmdline fallback). Do NOT re-add a try/except around .info.get() in delegate.py (dead code for an impossible scenario; delegate.py is out of this stage's scope anyway). Full POSIX suite green.

delegate.py IS legitimately in this stage's scope (already listed): it was changed during 3.2's window through the ledgered degraded window Q-0060-d847 (commit b82e237) — a real live-psutil balk-loop fix making the token process-scan degrade gracefully (eager process_iter(['environ']) raised SystemError on macOS and crashed every real delegation launch). That delegate.py change is DONE, verified against live psutil (2040-process scan, no crash), and must NOT be edited further by the worker. The REMAINING WORK for the worker is in factory/tests/test_gates.py: the 4 test_tagged_process_scan_* tests fail because the code now reads process.environ() lazily (a method) instead of the eager process_iter attr — update the test fakes to provide an environ() method (and raise from it for the denied/unreadable cases), so the tests exercise the new lazy per-candidate environ read. Full POSIX suite green.

Doctor psutil check stays subprocess-free in fast_status. LESSON: do NOT pr_ready before windows-hook-gates is green (WIN-2 premature-close).
